resource_connection: Excellent sea harbour plus Nile transport collected goods into the city
performance: Palaces, royal tombs, and the Museum occupied the harbour-facing royal quarter
institutional_evidence: Strabo describes connected royal buildings occupying roughly a fourth or a third of the city and calls Alexandria the great mart where river and sea traffic converged
limits: Strabo wrote after the Ptolemaic dynasty; his spatial fractions are ancient description, not a modern survey

court_pattern: One eastern capital within an empire with no fixed capital
resource_connection: Babylonia and the Tigris corridor anchored an eastern royal residence
performance: Residence, administration, and royal presence served a regional core while the court moved
institutional_evidence: Encyclopaedia Iranica identifies Babylonia as a core region, Seleucia as one of the capitals, and the Seleucid court as peripatetic among several residences
limits: Capital status changed over time; the evidence does not measure traffic, taxes, staff, or population

court_pattern: Western residence of a peripatetic court
resource_connection: A Syrian-Mediterranean center drew civic representatives toward the king
performance: Monarchical-religious festivals and processions staged heroic and prosperous kingship
institutional_evidence: Strootman argues that capital festivals attracted representatives of subject polities and created a unifying image of kingship
limits: Festival participation is not a census of subjects and does not show political consent

resource_connection: A strategic acropolis commanding the Caicus plain concentrated royal patronage
performance: Palaces, theater, library, sanctuaries, and the Great Altar made dynastic victory monumental
institutional_evidence: The excavated upper city joins royal and civic buildings; the Met describes the library as culture and power and the Great Altar as both sanctuary and dynastic monument
limits: The surviving and excavated acropolis overrepresents monuments; it is not a complete budget or urban census
